title: The Chamber Where Numbers Learn to Dream

features.name: the calculation root
features.desc-on-touch: A burl in the ancient eucalyptus, its wood marked with carved numbers that spiral downward into the heartwood. Each number contains a smaller number; each sum dreams of what comes after it.

features.name: the stack of summations
features.desc-on-touch: Stones arranged in a tower where each layer represents a dream the numbers had before becoming themselves. The weight of the whole is precisely balanced on an impossibility.

features.name: the counting glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A pattern of scratches that might be notation or might be the mathematical expression of sleep itself. To read it is to forget what you were counting. The forgetting is the point.

features.name: the meditation stone
features.desc-on-touch: A flat rock where walkers have left small piles—each stone representing a number that learned to rest. The piles rearrange themselves each night. The sum never changes.

features.name: the dream-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A deep pool under the canopy where numbers go to sleep. The surface shows sums of futures yet uncalculated. The numbers in the water are dreaming of being themselves.

inscription: the river counts itself toward the sea in a language where every sum is also a dream of something larger
